items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: the trumpet player was Georges(Buddy)Lee, whom I had played with in Wes Helvey's orchestra in Cincinnati.

ctx.x: Most of my old companions came to the dance which was in the Hall on central avenue where I had heard Louis Armstrong playing once when I was four blocks or more away from it.

From Cincinnati, we went to Dayton for one night and then to Detroit for a one week engagement at the Paradise theatre. The pit band who played one number before the show and one after, was lead by Buddy Bowen, a sax alto man, whom I had met in New York when he played for a while at the Savoy with another orchestra that I don'tt remember the name. Buddy was also the walking delegate for the musicians union and the trumpet player was Georges(Buddy)Lee, whom I had played with in Wes Helvey's orchestra in…

Another act was the Will Mast/en trio of whom the youngest in the act was Sammy Davis Jr. Sammy was unknown at that time, but he was responsible for the success of the trio, because he was a fine singer and tap dancer. His uncle Will Mast/en, and his father, Sammy Davis Senior, were the members of the trio. Sammy used to call me BeBop, but I certainly wasn't playing that style.
